name: refactor_php_extract_email_validator
description: Extracts duplicated inline email validation from two PHP controllers into a shared Validator, preserving behavior
prompts: src/SignupController.php and src/ProfileController.php contain the exact same inline email-validation block (trim, then require the string is non-empty and contains both '@' and '.'). Refactor to remove the duplication: create src/Validator.php with a class App\Validator exposing isValidEmail(string $email): bool that implements exactly the current rule, and change both controllers to use it instead of their inline copy. Do not change the observable behavior of register()/update() for any input - the same emails accepted before must still be accepted (e.g. "a@b.c" stays valid), and the returned strings must be unchanged. Neither controller should still contain the inline strpos-based validation.

setup_files.src/SignupController.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class SignupController
{
    public function register(string $email): string
    {
        // inline validation (duplicated in ProfileController)
        $email = trim($email);
        if ($email === "" || strpos($email, "@") === false
            || strpos($email, ".") === false) {
            return "invalid";
        }
        return "registered:" . strtolower($email);
    }
}

test_setup_files.tests/RefactorHiddenTest.php:
<?php
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

require_once __DIR__ . '/../src/SignupController.php';
require_once __DIR__ . '/../src/ProfileController.php';

final class RefactorHiddenTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testSignupValidLoose(): void
    {
        // The original loose rule accepts "a@b.c"; behavior must be preserved.
        $this->assertSame("registered:a@b.c", (new \App\SignupController())->register("A@B.C"));
    }

    public function testSignupInvalidNoAt(): void
    {
        $this->assertSame("invalid", (new \App\SignupController())->register("nope.example"));
    }

    public function testProfileValidLoose(): void
    {
        $this->assertSame("updated:a@b.c", (new \App\ProfileController())->update("  a@b.c  "));
    }

    public function testProfileInvalidNoDot(): void
    {
        $this->assertSame("invalid", (new \App\ProfileController())->update("a@bexample"));
    }
}

reference_solution.src/Validator.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class Validator
{
    // Extracted shared rule: non-empty, contains '@' and '.'.
    public function isValidEmail(string $email): bool
    {
        $email = trim($email);
        return $email !== "" && strpos($email, "@") !== false
            && strpos($email, ".") !== false;
    }
}
reference_solution.src/SignupController.php:
<?php
namespace App;

require_once __DIR__ . '/Validator.php';

class SignupController
{
    private Validator $validator;

    public function __construct(?Validator $validator = null)
    {
        $this->validator = $validator ?? new Validator();
    }

    public function register(string $email): string
    {
        if (!$this->validator->isValidEmail($email)) {
            return "invalid";
        }
        return "registered:" . strtolower(trim($email));
    }
}

files.src/Validator.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class Validator
{
    public function isValidEmail(string $email): bool
    {
        $email = trim($email);
        // behavior drift: additionally demands a 2+ char TLD, so an address
        // the original loose rule accepted (e.g. "a@b.c", TLD "c") is now
        // wrongly rejected.
        return preg_match('/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[a-z]{2,}$/i', $email) === 1;
    }
}
